newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: China raises metal exports to S.Korea for profits.
newsitem.headline: China raises metal exports to S.Korea for profits.

text.p: Chinese copper and zinc producers were seen recently increasing sales to South Korea to take advantage of current high prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders in Seoul said on Thursday.
"Recently, Chinese exporters are calling us frequently to check whether we are interested in Chinese metals," a trader with a major trading house said.
The trader said the copper purchase amount from China was limited at 500 tonnes to 1,000 tonnes per deal due to a slowdown in the domestic economy following a series of corporate collapses this year.
The domestic metal market will close on Friday for the Memorial Day holiday.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were unchanged at $93-$100 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME's cash prices, traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices fell to 1,540,000 won a tonne from 1,550,000 won a week ago.

LG Metals Corp, an affiliate of LG Group and South Korea's largest copper producer, raised its monthly domestic selling price early this week to 2,467,000 won a tonne for June, up 113,000 won from 2,354,000 won a month earlier.
Korea Zinc, the country's largest zinc and lead producer, also raised its monthly domestic zinc selling price by 65,000 won a tonne to 1,348,000 won from 1,283,000 won in May.
Korea Zinc's monthly lead price fell to 684,000 won a tonne from 708,000 won a month ago.
Both LG Metals' and Korea Zinc's prices reflect May's LME monthly cash average prices and benchmark for domestic physical trades.
